scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Debaa: Women’s Waves of Devotion in Mayotte
This is Debaa. 20th century.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Debaa originated in Mayotte in the 1920s-30s, introduced by a foundi from Anjouan linked to the Sufi Rifa'iyya brotherhood.
Initially a male religious ritual, it opened to women and became exclusively female.
It draws from Sufism, a spiritual tradition influenced by early Islamic asceticism, but Debaa uniquely incorporates dance alongside traditional Sufi chanting and percussion.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Debaa is performed for religious praise, especially for pilgrims to Mecca, during Ramadan as a rite of expiation, at Mawlid celebrations, weddings, and as a competitive display between village groups.
It also serves as a ritual of seduction for young women seeking suitors.
The dance embodies both sacred and profane elements, symbolizing female identity and social cohesion in Mayotte.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music consists of Arabic chants from sacred Islamic texts, often about the Prophet's birth, performed responsorially with a soloist and chorus.
Percussion instruments include simple drums and tambourines.
Listen for the tambourine, simple drums.

The music features a solo female voice chanting sacred Arabic texts, echoed by a female chorus, accompanied by steady, simple percussion like tambourines, creating a meditative yet rhythmic atmosphere.
